summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted after noticing dark stools and a small amount of bright red blood in the toilet, accompanied by lightheadedness and weakness. Her hemoglobin on admission was 9.7 g/dL, which was higher than her baseline, and remained stable throughout the stay. She had no signs of acute kidney injury or hepatic decompensation. Given her recent extensive negative GI workup and hemodynamic stability, further endoscopic procedures were not performed. She was managed with IV pantoprazole, temporary NPO status, and close monitoring. Her lactulose was adjusted, and diuretics were held pending outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue pantoprazole, resume baseline medications except diuretics, monitor for signs of active bleeding, and complete outpatient lab testing with results to be faxed to her liver specialist.
